page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The CPU includes a 50 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-assisted virtualization via Microsoft Hyper-V, alongside instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. It is bundled with 262 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position the E16s_v3 primarily in the average tier for multi-core and memory-bound operations, while single-core performance is relatively weak. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests fall into the middle 50% of benchmarked servers, as do Passmark CPU and memory scores. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, reaching 99.49 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 57.37 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Conversely, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 25%, indicating a tradeoff where parallelized workloads perform significantly better than single-core operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16s_v3 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require top-tier single-core CPU speeds. The server is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by its average Passmark database performance and Redis SET throughput of 11.37 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and light language model inference, such as text generation with small 135M or medium 7B models.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance, alongside weaker single-core capabilities.
